about.title: About the data
about.not_do: What the system does not do
about.not_do_items: It does not forecast landslides or predict when an event will happen.
It does not replace a geologist or an on-site inspection.
It does not claim that a place is free of risk.
It does not send alerts to the public.
about.does_text: It shows where the data differ from the norm of the same cell at a similar time of year, and which place a specialist should check. Displacement is measured along the satellite line of sight (LOS), not along the slope.
about.api_text: Displacement series, norms and product passports are available with an API key. OpenAPI docs: /docs.

land.kicker: NASA Space Apps · open satellite data
land.title: Satellite radar spots where slopes have started to move — before it is visible to the eye
land.sub: Slope Watch compares every place with its own norm using open NISAR / Sentinel-1 radar images and shows what to check first. It is not a forecast — a specialist makes the decision.
land.step1.d: Radar images the area every 12 days — through clouds and at night
land.step2.d: Each cell is compared with its own history at the same time of year
land.step3.d: Deviations become a short task list for specialists
land.why1.t: Sees through clouds and at night
land.why1.d: Radar illuminates the surface itself — mountain clouds do not stop it.
land.why2.d: Interferometry (InSAR) measures surface movement of the order of centimetres.
land.why3.d: NISAR / Sentinel-1 (ESA/Copernicus) images and NASA data are free for everyone.
land.honest: The system shows deviations from the norm. It is not a forecast and not a danger rating.
today.title: Today
today.line: Need checking: {n} · new since the previous image: {m} · data from {date}
today.empty: Today everything is within the norm. The next image is expected around {date}.
today.off_season: Radar displacement is not being measured right now: {reason}. Below are the results of the latest cycle with data ({date}).
today.off_reason: the data are out of date or the place is under snow
today.map_hint: Click a task — the map zooms to the place
tour.admin.1: This is your task list: places where the radar sees a deviation from the norm. The most important are on top.
tour.admin.2: The map shows the same places. Colour is the status; grey means there is not enough data.
tour.admin.3: Open a task to see the chart, a plain-language explanation and what we do not know.
tour.admin.4: Your main action is “Pass to a specialist”. The system does not forecast and does not decide for people.
tour.mchs.1: Tasks are sorted by priority: red first, then new ones.
tour.mchs.2: The map shows statuses; the time slider scrolls through past images.
tour.mchs.3: Inside a task: chart with the norm band; rules and numbers are under “More for specialists”.
tour.mchs.4: After a field check mark “Confirmed” or “False alarm” — this goes back into the system.
tour.other.1: Use the top menu to switch between sections.
tour.other.2: Switch between real NISAR / Sentinel-1 data and demo data here.
tour.other.3: Choose the interface language: RU, KY or EN.
tour.other.4: Press “?” at any time to see these hints again.
g.insar.d: Radar interferometry: comparing two images of the same place shows how far the surface has moved.
g.los.d: Movement towards or away from the satellite — not the same as movement down the slope.
g.coherence.d: How similar two images are at one point. Low coherence (snow, water, forest) means the measurement cannot be trusted.
g.norm.d: How this place usually behaves at the same time of year in past years.
g.mad.d: Median absolute deviation — a robust measure of usual spread that single outliers do not distort.
g.provisional.d: A preliminary product version: the data may be reprocessed.
g.backscatter.d: Brightness of the radar echo. A sharp change means the surface changed (debris, water, snow).

ba.title: Before / after — radar
ba.hint: Sentinel-1 radar brightness (γ⁰ VV). Drag the curtain: brighter means stronger echo (rock, debris), darker means smooth water or wet snow.
ba.none: Backscatter images are available in the “Real data” mode.
near.title: Nearby (500 m)
near.not_computed: The “Nearby” layer has not been computed yet
retro.title: Check on the past
retro.intro: Why the system can be trusted: we look at what it showed during the 6 months before known events. Thresholds were not tuned to the events; the norm uses past years only.
retro.reason.mostly_grey: data were insufficient most of the time (snow, low coherence)
retro.reason.no_deviation: the radar saw no deviation — the event may have developed faster than the image cycle or outside the satellite's line of sight
retro.reason.event_outside_grid: the event is outside the cell grid
retro.none: Open catalogues (NASA Global Landslide Catalog) list no events at this object for the data period. The check can be run once the MES provides a list of events; the result will be shown here without tuning.
retro.false: Alerts far from any event: {a} of {t} evaluated statuses ({p}%)
retro.timeline: Statuses for 180 days before the event (worst in the cell and neighbours)
story.title: Demo story
story.s1: Slope Watch: the NISAR / Sentinel-1 radar watches slopes where people can hardly get.
story.s2: The “Today” screen: only what needs checking, by priority.
story.s3: A red place: movement above the norm for several cycles and in neighbouring cells.
story.s4: Inside: a chart with the norm band and a plain-language explanation. It is not a forecast.
story.s5: Time machine: slow slope movement over a season becomes visible.
story.s6: One button: “Pass to a specialist”. A person always decides.
story.s7: Check on the past: what the system showed before known events — honestly, without tuning.
today.off_reason_glacier: the glacier and slopes are under snow; radar displacement is measured in the snow-free season (≈ June–September)
today.empty_off: No deviations from the norm in the latest cycle with data ({date}). Cells with not enough data: {grey} of {n} — this does not mean “within norm”.
